# EPSS · CISA KEV · Vulnrichment — the exploitability feeds

The two ground-truth/prediction feeds the gate joins on, plus the free SSVC inputs. All are public, no-auth,
daily, and small enough to cache once per pipeline.

## EPSS v5 — exploitation-likelihood

**Model:** EPSS **v5**, released 2026-06-15 (23% better than v4; scores all 318k+ published CVEs). The
machine-readable identifier is **`model_version: v2026.06.15`** (line 1 of every CSV). Governed by the
**FIRST EPSS SIG but generated by Empirical Security** — cite v5 in prose, `v2026.06.15` in a reproducibility
stamp. The production model is **not retrained daily**; scores move because the ~2,850 features move.

**Meaning:** probability the CVE is exploited **in the wild in the next 30 days** (0–1). `percentile` is the
relative rank among currently-scored CVEs. Published daily, typically within ~2 min after 13:30 UTC.

### The bulk CSV — prefer this for any CI gate

```bash
curl -sL -o epss.csv.gz https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz     # ~2.5 MB gz, ~360k rows
curl -sL -o e.gz        https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-2026-08-15.csv.gz  # a pinned day (archive → 2021-04-14)
# Line 1: #model_version:v2026.06.15,score_date:...   Line 2: cve,epss,percentile
```

One request, no batching traps, no rate-limit exposure, offline-reproducible. The old `epss.cyentia.com`
301-redirects to `epss.empiricalsecurity.com`.

### The API — single lookups / small batches only

Base `https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss`, no auth, `Cache-Control: max-age=86400`.

```bash
curl -s "https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss?cve=CVE-2021-44228"
# {"data":[{"cve":"CVE-2021-44228","epss":"0.999990000","percentile":"1.000000000","date":"2026-08-16"}]}
```

| Param | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `cve=` | single or comma-separated batch |
| `date=YYYY-MM-DD` | historical pin |
| `epss-gt` / `epss-lt` / `percentile-gt` / `percentile-lt` | range filters |
| `offset` / `limit` | pagination (`limit` default 100) |
| `order=!epss` | sort (`!` = descending) |
| `scope=time-series` | adds a 30-entry `time-series[]` |
| `envelope=false` | bare array |

> **Two silent-failure traps — cache the CSV to avoid both:**
> 1. **Scores are JSON strings** (`"0.999990000"`) — always cast to float.
> 2. **An oversized batch returns HTTP 200 with `total:0`, not an error** (fails above ~140 CVEs). Batch at
>    **≤100** and **assert the returned row count**. Unknown/malformed CVEs are **silently dropped**, so a
>    short response is ambiguous — treat a missing CVE as `epss=None`, never `0`.
> 3. `days=` is broken (returns `total:0`); avoid. `q=` is fuzzy substring; avoid.

### Thresholds (FIRST guidance + measured coverage)

FIRST prescribes no universal threshold and gives CVSS-migration equivalents: **90th percentile (≈0.04)** ≈
the effort of "CVSS Critical" (~10% of CVEs); **0.008** ≈ "CVSS High-and-above" (~48%). Only **1.5–3%** of
CVEs are exploited in any 30-day window. Measured against today's feed (360,399 CVEs) + today's KEV (1,665):

| EPSS ≥ | % corpus | KEV recall |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 1.20% | 51.8% |
| 0.2 | 2.79% | 67.2% |
| **0.1** | **4.80%** | **76.3%** |
| 0.04 | 10.35% | 86.2% |

`EPSS ≥ 0.1` is the common gate — but it **misses 24% of KEV** (one exploited CVE sits at 0.0025). That gap
is the empirical reason KEV is a separate branch.

## CISA KEV — exploited-in-the-wild ground truth

```bash
curl -sO https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json   # 1.6 MB — note /feeds/
curl -sO https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/csv/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.csv      # note the ASYMMETRIC /csv/
# envelope: {"catalogVersion":"2026.08.14","dateReleased":"...","count":1665,"vulnerabilities":[...]}
```

**Schema (draft-07).** Per-vuln **required:** `cveID`, `vendorProject`, `product`, `vulnerabilityName`,
`dateAdded`, `shortDescription`, `requiredAction`, `dueDate`. **Optional:** `knownRansomwareCampaignUse`
(`"Known"` | `"Unknown"` — a **string**, test `== "Known"`, never truthiness), `notes`, `cwes[]` (newer, may
be absent).

> **BOD 26-04 (2026-06-10) superseded the revoked BOD 22-01.** The live feed proves it — every
> `requiredAction` now cites BOD 26-04, and CISA now sets `dueDate` *before* `dateAdded+14`. Say BOD 26-04,
> not BOD 22-01. Inclusion criteria unchanged: assigned CVE + reliable active-exploitation evidence + a clear
> remediation.

**Membership test — load once into a set, never per-CVE HTTP:**

```python
kev = {v["cveID"]: v for v in json.load(open("kev.json"))["vulnerabilities"]}
hit = kev.get("CVE-2021-44228")   # {'dateAdded':'2021-12-10','knownRansomwareCampaignUse':'Known', ...}
```

**Optional widening — VulnCheck KEV** (free *with registration*, claims ~80% more exploited CVEs than CISA,
and is an EPSS input): `https://api.vulncheck.com/v3/index/vulncheck-kev` (401 without a token). Position as
an opt-in widening of the KEV branch; **CISA KEV stays the no-auth default.**

## CISA Vulnrichment — free SSVC inputs per CVE

`github.com/cisagov/vulnrichment` (layout `2024/35xxx/CVE-2024-35057.json`) publishes SSVC into the CVE's ADP
container for every CVE id:

```json
"options": [{"Exploitation":"poc"},{"Automatable":"yes"},{"Technical Impact":"total"}]
```

`Automatable` (yes/no) and `Technical Impact` (partial/total) are the two BOD-26-04 gate inputs that a CVSS
base score is *not* — free, official, per-CVE. Use them to tighten the ATTEND branch
(`AND Automatable == yes`). `Exploitation` (none/poc/active) corroborates KEV.

## Rules

- Prefer the **EPSS CSV** for a CI gate (no API traps); cast scores to float; missing CVE → `None`.
- Load **KEV once into a set**; `knownRansomwareCampaignUse == "Known"` (string); cite **BOD 26-04**.
- Record `model_version` (`v2026.06.15`) + KEV `catalogVersion` in every report — the same CVE changes
  verdict day to day.
- Vulnrichment `Automatable`/`Technical Impact` are better gate inputs than CVSS base score.
